frontMatter.introduction:
Welcome to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual for Kraftwares India Pvt. Ltd. This document serves as a comprehensive guide for employees and stakeholders, outlining the standardized processes and procedures essential for the efficient and consistent operation of our business.

At Kraftwares, we are committed to upholding the highest standards of quality, safety, and efficiency across all functions of our organization. This SOP manual is designed to provide clear, structured, and practical instructions for performing various tasks within the company, ensuring that our operations run smoothly, consistently, and in compliance with all relevant regulatory requirements.

The procedures outlined in this manual are critical to maintaining the integrity of our products, services, and business relationships. It is our goal to ensure all employees understand and adhere to these guidelines to foster an environment of continuous improvement, accountability, and excellence.

Driving sustainability, empowering communities, and upholding ethical excellence—this manual provides a clear framework for integrating responsible business practices into the core operations of Kraftwares India Pvt. Ltd., reinforcing our commitment to long-term growth and positive impact.

blocks.text: This Energy efficiency and emissions reduction SOP presents Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.’s structured approach to managing and optimizing energy consumption across its manufacturing and operational activities. The approach focuses on improving energy efficiency through the use of energy-efficient equipment, process optimization, preventive maintenance practices, and the adoption of resource conservation measures to minimize environmental impacts and enhance operational performance.

Additional measures include monitoring energy consumption patterns, identifying energy-saving opportunities, promoting efficient use of utilities, and encouraging employee participation in energy conservation initiatives. This SOP supports Kraftwares’ broader ESG objectives by fostering continuous improvement in energy performance, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements, reducing energy-related costs, and contributing to the responsible use of natural resources.

To provide a standardized approach for managing and optimizing energy consumption across Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.’s operations. This SOP aims to promote efficient energy use, reduce environmental impacts associated with energy consumption, improve operational efficiency, and support the company’s sustainability and ESG objectives.

This SOP applies to all facilities, departments, processes, and equipment within Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. where energy resources are utilized during routine business operations. It covers activities related to manufacturing, assembly, utilities, warehousing, packaging, storage, administrative functions, and other supporting operational areas that contribute to overall energy consumption.
The following procedures outline Kraftwares' approach as a part of energy management, focusing on sustainable practices, energy optimization, and carbon emission reduction.

body.text: The installed rooftop solar PV system is equipped with advanced monitoring software that continuously tracks:

Real-time energy generation and cumulative output.
System efficiency and panel performance trends.
Deviations from expected parameters, such as voltage irregularities or sudden output drops.
Alerts are automatically triggered in the event of system anomalies, enabling prompt diagnostics and corrective measures.

Solar Panel Cleaning: Carried out at regular intervals (e.g., monthly), depending on local environmental conditions. This ensures removal of dust, dirt, bird droppings, or debris that can obstruct sunlight and reduce efficiency.
Component Inspection: Routine inspections are conducted for:
Inverters and Junction Boxes – checked for faults, overheating, or signs of internal wear.
Cabling and Connectors – examined for physical damage, corrosion, or loose connections.
Mounting Structures – assessed for structural integrity, rust, and anchoring stability.

Any deviations or underperformance identified by the monitoring system are immediately reported to the maintenance team.
On-site diagnostics are carried out to identify issues such as:
Malfunctioning inverters or failed modules.
Faulty connectors, wiring damage, or panel shading.
Identified faults are promptly addressed through repair or component replacement using certified parts, ensuring minimal system downtime.

steps.heading: Health, Safety, and Risk Control Measures

body.text:
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): All personnel engaged in maintenance activities are required to wear appropriate PPE, including electrical-grade gloves, helmets, eye protection, non-conductive footwear, and harnesses for rooftop access.
Lockout/Tagout (LOTO): Strict LOTO procedures are followed before performing maintenance to eliminate the risk of electrical shock or unintended activation.
Fire Safety Compliance: Electrical installations are maintained in accordance with fire safety norms. Appropriate fire extinguishers (Class C-rated) are readily available near control panels and inverter stations.
Comprehensive records are maintained covering:

Daily, weekly, and monthly energy production data.
Scheduled maintenance, cleaning logs, and fault resolutions.
System performance trends and deviation reports.
Regulatory Compliance:

Operations align with the Electricity Act, 2003, CEA Safety Regulations, and relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) for solar installations.
Periodic internal audits are conducted to ensure continued compliance and system optimization.
Kraftwares continually invests in technology upgrades and process optimisation to enhance energy efficiency. This includes:

Kraftwares’ key manufacturing operations, including metal forming, polishing, finishing, assembly, and packaging processes, utilize modern equipment and machinery designed to support efficient energy utilization and optimize operational performance.
Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) ensure motors and equipment operate at optimal energy levels, reducing power consumption during low-load conditions and improving overall operational efficiency.
Older, high-energy-consuming machinery is systematically replaced with BEE-rated or equivalent certified equipment to improve overall energy efficiency.

steps.heading: Automated Process Management and Operational Controls

body.text:
Automated controls and monitoring systems are integrated into key manufacturing and utility operations to regulate equipment performance based on operational requirements.
Equipment operations are monitored and controlled based on production requirements and load conditions, enabling machines to operate efficiently and minimizing idle running and unnecessary energy consumption.
Operational activities are planned and coordinated to ensure equipment is utilized efficiently, thereby optimizing runtime, improving productivity, and reducing energy usage.

steps.heading: Energy Management and Preventive Maintenance System

body.text:
Critical machinery, including manufacturing equipment, polishing units, packaging equipment, compressors, lighting systems, and utility equipment, is periodically monitored to assess energy consumption, operational efficiency, and potential abnormalities.
The Maintenance and Operations teams review equipment performance and energy consumption data on a regular basis to identify inefficiencies or abnormal energy usage patterns.
Preventive maintenance schedules are aligned with operational and energy performance requirements to:
Maintain optimal equipment operation.
Prevent overheating, mechanical wear, leakages, and inefficiencies arising from misalignment, inadequate maintenance, or ageing components.
Extend the operational lifespan of equipment, thereby reducing resource consumption and the environmental impact associated with frequent replacements.

All conventional fluorescent, incandescent, and halogen lighting systems have been replaced with energy-efficient LED fixtures across production areas, packaging sections, warehouses, and administrative offices.
LEDs are selected for their high lumen-per-watt efficiency and extended service life, ensuring optimal illumination with reduced power consumption.
This upgrade has contributed to noticeable reductions in lighting-related energy usage, along with lower maintenance requirements.

Motion sensors are installed in low-traffic areas such as storage rooms, corridors, utility areas, and restrooms, ensuring that lighting is activated only when required.
Daylight sensors are positioned near windows and skylights to automatically dim or switch off artificial lighting when adequate natural light is available.
Together, these sensor-based systems help prevent unnecessary energy consumption during non-operational hours and daylight conditions.

The facility is divided into independent lighting zones based on operational areas and occupancy schedules. For example:
Production and packaging areas operate on extended schedules.
Storage, dispatch, and utility areas follow reduced lighting cycles.
Smart control systems utilise programmable timers and real-time inputs to dynamically adjust lighting intensity and duration based on:
Occupancy sensors
Time-of-day settings
Availability of natural light
Emergency and exit lighting systems remain excluded from automated controls to ensure continuous compliance with safety requirements.

steps.heading: Heat Recovery and Thermal Energy Optimization

body.text:
The diesel generator (DG) sets at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. generate significant thermal energy from engine exhaust gases and the coolant system during operation.
This heat is recovered using exhaust gas heat exchangers, which extract thermal energy from high-temperature exhaust streams.
The recovered thermal energy is utilised for preheating process water and supporting manufacturing and utility operations where applicable.
Utilisation of recovered heat reduces dependence on external fuel-based heating systems, thereby lowering overall energy consumption and associated carbon emissions.

All hot water and steam pipelines connected to DG set heat recovery systems are fitted with high-quality insulation to minimize thermal losses.
Insulation helps maintain consistent process temperatures, shortens heating cycle times, and improves overall thermal efficiency.

By reusing internally generated heat, the system reduces reliance on external heating systems such as electric boilers or fossil-fuel-based heaters.
This results in:
Lower energy consumption
Reduced fuel usage
A measurable decrease in carbon dioxide emissions
The initiative directly supports Kraftwares sustainability and decarbonization goals, aligning with both internal targets and external environmental compliance frameworks

steps.heading: Transition to Cleaner Fuels and Emission Control

body.text:
Where technically feasible, Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. evaluates and transitions to cleaner fuel alternatives for utility operations, reducing reliance on conventional fossil fuels across production and processing areas.
Where cleaner fuel alternatives are adopted, fuel selection follows established environmental criteria to support consistent combustion efficiency and minimize environmental impact.
Utility and heating systems are integrated into daily production schedules, providing stable and reliable energy for manufacturing operations and associated facility activities.
Boiler operations follow optimized fuel usage protocols, which are consistently applied to maximize energy efficiency and maintain process reliability.
Fuel consumption, emissions, and thermal efficiency are continuously monitored to ensure optimal boiler performance.
Scheduled audits and routine maintenance are carried out to maintain consistent operation and prevent energy wastage.
The use of biomass fuel has resulted in measurable reductions in CO₂, SO₂, and particulate matter emissions.
Improved fuel efficiency contributes to reduced operating costs while sustaining production capacity.
These practices support Kraftwares ongoing decarbonization and sustainability initiatives.

steps.heading: Installation of Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS)

body.text:
All new combustion systems are equipped with continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) that provide real-time data on:
Stack emissions (CO₂, NOₓ, SOₓ, and particulate matter)
Combustion temperature and efficiency
These systems allow the engineering team to:
Adjust air-to-fuel ratios dynamically for clean combustion
Detect abnormal pollutant levels early
Maintain compliance with national and state-level pollution control norms

Routine energy and emissions audits are carried out quarterly by the EHS and engineering teams to:
Evaluate combustion performance
Identify maintenance needs
Recommend tuning or retrofitting where efficiency drops are observed
All findings are documented in boiler performance logs and used to update the facility’s energy management action plan.

blocks.text: To systematically assess and enhance energy efficiency across all the operations regular energy audits are conducted, focusing on identifying conservation opportunities and improving system performance.

body.text:
The energy audit is scheduled once in a three-year block, in coordination with an authorized third-party energy audit firm.
Key energy systems and equipment at Kraftwares, including manufacturing equipment, polishing machines, hydraulic presses, power presses, air compressors, utility systems, pumps, motors, DG sets, material handling equipment, and lighting systems, are identified in advance for detailed evaluation to optimize energy efficiency and support the company’s sustainability initiatives.
The operation and maintenance teams are notified about the schedule and their roles in supporting data sharing, equipment access, and on-ground coordination.
Historical energy data, including electricity bills, operational logs, and equipment specifications, are compiled to establish baseline performance.

Real-time parameters such as voltage, current, power factor, temperature, and load are measured using calibrated instruments.
Energy consumption records are collected for a period of 12 months to analyze trends in demand, unit consumption, and billing charges.
Details of equipment load, usage hours, operating efficiency, and power system layout are recorded across departments.
Special focus is given to air compressors, pumps, motors, DG sets, and manufacturing equipment, where potential inefficiencies or energy loss are commonly observed.

All measured and recorded data is analyzed to identify energy losses, low-efficiency equipment, and systems with potential for upgrades.
Equipment such as air compressors, pumps, motors, DG sets, transformers, and other utility systems are evaluated for loading efficiency and specific power consumption.
Power quality assessments, such as harmonics analysis and power factor checks, are conducted to evaluate system stability and penalties.

The audit findings are compiled into a detailed Energy Audit Report, which includes:
Energy Conservation Measures (EnCon)
Cost-benefit analysis
Estimated savings in kWh and ₹
Required investment and payback periods

All approved recommendations are scheduled for phased implementation.
The plant team integrates energy-efficient solutions identified through the audit process.
Post-implementation monitoring is conducted to compare actual performance against projections.
A summary of improvements is maintained for regulatory compliance and internal review.
Carbon Footprint Calculation:

Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. undertakes comprehensive carbon footprint assessments to quantify and manage its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The calculation process follows internationally recognized standards, primarily the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and global comparability. Emissions are systematically categorized into:

Scope 1 – Direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company, such as emissions from generators, and manufacturing equipment.
Scope 2 – Indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity, steam, or other forms of imported energy used in production and administrative operations.
Scope 3 – Other indirect emissions that occur in the value chain, including emissions from upstream activities (e.g., raw material transportation, supplier emissions) and downstream activities (e.g., product distribution, waste disposal, and employee commuting).

To support this process, Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. maintains energy consumption data, production volumes, transport logs, and supplier information. These data points are used to calculate CO₂-equivalent emissions across all scopes. Regular third-party carbon audits are performed to monitor emissions trends over time, assess progress toward emission reduction targets, and identify opportunities for further energy efficiency or cleaner technologies. These audits also aid in maintaining regulatory compliance, improving environmental transparency, and guiding sustainability initiatives across operations.

By embedding carbon footprint calculations into its environmental management system, Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. strengthens its strategic approach to sustainability and reaffirms its commitment to mitigating climate change.

Regular training sessions are held to engage employees in identifying energy-saving opportunities, adopting energy-efficient practices, and reducing wastage in daily operations. This ensures that energy management practices are embedded within the company culture.

Key indicators such as energy consumption, emissions, and machine performance are assessed to identify gaps and areas for enhancement. Findings are shared with the management team and relevant departments. Where required, corrective actions are implemented to further optimize resource use and reduce the facility’s carbon footprint.

The Water Conservation and Management Procedure sets out the framework adopted by Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. to optimize water consumption, enhance conservation efforts, and promote responsible water use across its manufacturing and operational activities. It includes measures for monitoring water usage, implementing water-saving practices, and improving water efficiency through appropriate technologies and operational controls. Regular water audits are conducted to identify inefficiencies and support continuous improvement, while routine inspection and maintenance of water infrastructure help prevent leakages and water loss. Through these measures, Kraftwares aims to strengthen water stewardship, support sustainability objectives, and ensure the responsible use of natural resources.

The objective of this SOP is to establish a systematic approach for the efficient use, conservation, and management of water resources at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. It aims to optimize water consumption, promote responsible water usage across manufacturing and operational activities, and ensure effective monitoring and control of water-related processes within the facility.

This SOP applies to all water-related activities within Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.’s manufacturing and operational facilities. It covers water usage in manufacturing processes, cleaning and housekeeping activities, utility operations, sanitation facilities, and other supporting functions, along with the monitoring, conservation, and water management measures implemented across the organization.

body.text:
The operations, maintenance, and EHS teams conduct routine inspections of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) units, including feed tanks, pumps, pipelines, valves, and storage tanks prior to operation.
Operators verify that chemical dosing systems, pH adjustment units, and treatment chemicals are available and functioning properly.
Safety personnel confirm the availability of personal protective equipment (PPE), spill containment materials, and emergency response equipment.
Wastewater Monitoring

Wastewater generated from manufacturing processes, equipment cleaning activities, utility operations, and domestic usage is collected and routed to the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) for treatment.
Key parameters such as pH, temperature, TDS, COD, and flow rates are monitored regularly to ensure effective treatment performance and compliance with applicable requirements.
Effluent Treatment

Wastewater generated from manufacturing and utility operations is treated through a multi-stage treatment process within the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP). These stages include primary treatment for removal of suspended solids, secondary biological treatment for degradation of organic matter, and tertiary treatment for further purification and polishing of the treated effluent.
Chemical dosing is carried out in controlled quantities within the treatment system to facilitate neutralization, coagulation, and flocculation processes, ensuring effective removal of suspended contaminants and impurities.
Air blowers and mixing systems are operated as required to maintain proper aeration and support efficient treatment performance.
Treated effluent is regularly monitored for parameters such as pH, COD, TDS, and suspended solids to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory standards. Any deviation in treatment efficiency is reported to the responsible personnel, and corrective actions are implemented promptly.
Water Recovery and Reuse

Treated water suitable for reuse is stored in designated storage tanks and reused for non-potable applications such as floor cleaning, gardening, utility washing, and other auxiliary activities wherever feasible.
Sludge and other treatment residues generated during the treatment process are handled, stored, and disposed of in accordance with applicable environmental regulations and approved waste management procedures.
Sampling & Testing
Treated water is sampled periodically and analyzed for parameters such as pH, COD, TDS, and suspended solids to verify compliance with internal standards and regulatory limits.

Any deviation in treatment performance or water quality is immediately reported to the Environmental Compliance Officer (ECO).
Corrective actions may include adjusting chemical dosing, modifying operational parameters, conducting equipment maintenance, or increasing monitoring frequency.
All deviations and corrective actions are recorded and reviewed to ensure effective resolution.

Operators ensure that tanks, pumps, pipelines, treatment units, and surrounding work areas are maintained in a clean condition after operations.
Shutdown procedures for the ETP system are carried out according to established operational guidelines.
Daily records of operational parameters, water quality results, and maintenance activities are maintained.
Maintenance Schedule Table:

In case of ETP malfunction, overflow, pipeline leakage, or accidental spillage, operators shall initiate emergency shutdown and containment measures.
The EHS department and concerned personnel shall be notified immediately, and corrective measures shall be implemented.
Incident details shall be documented, investigated, and reviewed to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.

Treated water recovered through the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) is utilized for various non-potable applications within the facility to promote efficient water utilization and reduce dependence on freshwater sources.
Typical reuse applications include:

Cooling Systems: Treated water recovered from the ETP is utilized in cooling systems to support operational requirements and reduce dependence on freshwater sources.
Cleaning, Housekeeping, and Utility Applications: Recovered water is used for floor washing, cleaning of operational areas, equipment exterior cleaning, washing of containers, maintenance activities, and other non-potable utility and housekeeping requirements within the facility, thereby reducing freshwater consumption.
Gardening and Landscaping: Treated water is utilized for irrigation of green areas, landscaping, and plantation activities within the facility premises wherever feasible.

Recycled water is allocated based on operational requirements and quality suitability. Storage tanks, transfer pipelines, and valves are inspected regularly to ensure safe handling and prevent contamination. All reuse volumes are recorded in the Water Reuse Log Sheet, and any deviation in quality or supply is reported to the responsible supervisor for corrective action.

steps.heading: Reduction in Water Consumption and Waste water Generation
Operational Water Efficiency Measures for water consumption reduction

body.text:
Regular assessments of water usage are conducted by the Maintenance Team and Environmental Manager to identify opportunities for improving water efficiency in cleaning, degreasing, rinsing, surface treatment, and equipment sanitation activities.
High-pressure washing systems are utilized in equipment cleaning, surface preparation, vehicle washing, and facility cleaning activities to achieve effective cleaning while minimizing water consumption. In addition, cleaning schedules and operational practices are optimized to prevent unnecessary water usage.
Only biodegradable cleaning agents, such as citrus-based cleaners and vinegar-based solutions, are employed where applicable. These cleaning agents facilitate effective cleaning while reducing the need for excessive rinsing and minimizing environmental impacts.
Water consumption trends are periodically monitored and reviewed to identify inefficiencies, implement corrective actions, and support continuous improvement in water conservation practices across the facility.

Regular assessments are conducted to identify opportunities for reducing wastewater generation from quenching, deburring, polishing, electro-polishing, rinsing, and other finishing operations.
Optimized water jets and controlled process parameters are utilized in deburring and finishing activities to ensure effective performance while minimizing wastewater generation.
Closed-loop systems are utilized in various manufacturing and finishing operations, including polishing, deburring, electro-polishing, and rinsing after coating, to recirculate water, reduce the total wastewater generation, and conserve resources. These systems are regularly monitored to ensure their effectiveness and efficiency.
Wastewater generation trends from finishing operations are periodically reviewed, and improvement measures are implemented to enhance process efficiency, reduce wastewater volumes, and support the company's water conservation and environmental management objectives.

To reduce dependency on groundwater and promote sustainable water use practices in line with government regulations, Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. has implemented a robust rainwater harvesting system integrated into its facility infrastructure.

Strategic Rooftop Collection: Rainwater is collected from the extensive rooftop surfaces of production blocks, utility areas, and administrative buildings. These rooftops have been structurally designed or modified to ensure optimal water flow towards dedicated collection points without interference from exhaust outlets.
First-Flush Diverter Mechanism: To ensure clean water collection, the first 2–3 mm of rainfall, which may contain dust, bird droppings, and other rooftop contaminants, is automatically diverted through a first-flush diverter system. This mechanism protects the storage tanks from initial impurities, ensuring better water quality for reuse.
Storage and Filtration Infrastructure: Post-diversion, the cleaner rainwater is routed through gravel and sand-based filtration units and stored in underground RCC tanks built with protective coatings to prevent leaching or microbial growth. These tanks are fitted with level indicators, overflow protection, and maintenance access points.
Applications of Harvested Rainwater: The stored rainwater is used for various non-potable industrial and facility-related purposes, including:
Cooling Tower Make-Up Water: Reduces demand on treated fresh water by supplementing cooling needs during high-load operations.
Toilet Flushing in Administrative and Production Areas: Helps save large volumes of water used in sanitary operations.
Landscape Irrigation: Ensures greener premises and cleaner surroundings without using borewell water.

Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. utilizes water-efficient cooling systems, to minimize water consumption and enhance operational efficiency. Traditional once-through cooling systems consumed significant quantities of freshwater and resulted in considerable water losses, whereas closed-loop cooling systems continuously recirculate the same cooling medium, reducing overall water demand.
The cooling systems operate by circulating water between cooling equipment, heat exchangers, and associated utility systems in a closed circuit, ensuring minimal water loss except for limited make-up water requirements. These systems contribute to reducing the facility’s freshwater consumption while supporting reliable cooling performance across manufacturing and utility operations.
Where technically feasible, treated water from the facility's wastewater treatment system may be utilized as make-up water for cooling applications, further promoting water reuse and resource conservation.
The cooling systems are designed to operate efficiently under varying operational loads, ensuring consistent performance with optimized water and energy usage. Routine monitoring, inspections, and preventive maintenance activities are conducted to maintain cooling efficiency, system reliability, and effective resource utilization.

Treated water intended for reuse in applications such as gardening, housekeeping activities, sanitation systems, or cooling operations is routinely monitored to ensure compliance with internal quality requirements and operational suitability.
Detailed records are maintained for all sampling and testing activities, including sample logs, laboratory reports, treatment system observations, and corrective actions taken in response to non-conformities. These records support internal reviews, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement initiatives.

This SOP establishes the standardized system followed by Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. for the identification, labelling, storage, handling, transportation, and reduction of hazardous substances used during manufacturing and supporting operations. It ensures safe operations, regulatory compliance, and minimization of environmental, health, and safety risks associated with hazardous materials.

To define clear procedures for hazard identification, labelling, safe storage, controlled handling, secure transportation, and compliant disposal of hazardous substances, while promoting the reduction of hazardous material usage and encouraging the adoption of safer alternatives wherever feasible.

This SOP applies to all locations where hazardous chemicals, cleaning agents, surface treatment chemicals, paints, coatings, adhesives, oils, lubricants, compressed gases, and other hazardous materials are procured, stored, transferred, handled, used, or disposed of within Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.

body.text:
All incoming hazardous materials are evaluated using Safety Data Sheets (SDS), GHS hazard symbols, manufacturer specifications, and chemical composition details.
Each hazardous material is labelled immediately upon receipt with:
Labels must remain clear, legible, and intact throughout the material lifecycle.
Every hazardous material is recorded in the hazardous material inventory system to ensure proper tracking and traceability.

Hazard classification (GHS pictograms)

Storage location

body.text:
Hazardous materials are stored only in designated, well-ventilated storage areas equipped with spill containment measures and appropriate fire protection systems.
Incompatible materials are strictly segregated (e.g., acids away from alkalis, oxidizers away from combustible materials, and flammable substances away from ignition sources).
Storage areas include:
Materials are arranged using the First-Expiry-First-Out (FEFO) principle wherever applicable.

Secondary containment trays

Mandatory PPE includes chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, face shields, masks or respirators (where required), and protective clothing.
Chemical handling activities are carried out in adequately ventilated areas to minimize employee exposure.
Emergency response equipment such as eyewash stations, spill kits, fire extinguishers, and first-aid facilities are maintained at accessible locations.
Controlled dispensing methods and measured quantities are used wherever feasible to minimize material wastage and exposure risks.

Internal movement of hazardous materials is controlled through documented material movement procedures to ensure traceability and accountability.
Hazardous materials are transported in sealed, properly labelled containers designed to prevent spills, leaks, or accidental release.
Appropriate trolleys, pallets, or carriers with spill containment features are used during internal transportation.
External transportation of hazardous materials or hazardous waste is conducted only through authorized transporters in accordance with applicable legal requirements.
Records of material movement, including quantities issued, receiving departments, dates, and responsible personnel, are maintained and reviewed periodically.

Preference is given to:

Procurement, Production, Quality, and EHS teams collaborate regularly to identify opportunities for replacing hazardous substances with safer alternatives.

Hazardous waste is stored in designated hazardous waste storage areas equipped with spill containment systems and hazard signage.
Disposal is carried out only through authorized hazardous waste recyclers, treatment facilities, or disposal agencies in accordance with applicable environmental regulations.
Waste manifests, disposal certificates, transportation records, and related compliance documents are maintained as per statutory retention requirements.

sops.title: Air pollution control and emission monitoring

blocks.text:
The Air Pollution Control and emission monitoring Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. outlines the measures implemented to manage air emissions generated from manufacturing, finishing, utility, and other operational activities. The procedure focuses on monitoring emission sources, maintaining air pollution control equipment, and ensuring effective operation of ventilation and emission control systems.

The SOP also includes periodic emissions monitoring, routine equipment inspections, preventive maintenance, and corrective actions where required. These practices help maintain controlled emission levels, ensure regulatory compliance, and support responsible environmental management across the facility.

Objective:
To implement effective strategies and control measures to prevent and minimize air emissions and other associated environmental impacts arising from manufacturing, finishing, utility, and supporting operations at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.

This SOP applies to the management and control of air emissions arising from manufacturing and utility operations at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. It covers the monitoring and control of particulate matter, dust, fumes, process emissions, odor, and operational noise generated during manufacturing, finishing, packaging, and supporting activities, including the use of emission control and ventilation systems.

substeps.text: Wet Scrubbers at Process Vents and Boilers: Wet scrubbers are installed at designated process exhaust systems at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. to capture and neutralize air pollutants generated during manufacturing operations. These systems help control emissions such as fumes, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), dust-laden air, and other process-related airborne contaminants that may arise during metal finishing, polishing, coating, and fuel combustion activities. The exhaust gases pass through a scrubbing solution, which reacts with and removes harmful components before the treated gases are released into the atmosphere, ensuring emissions remain within applicable regulatory limits. The scrubbers operate during relevant process operations, with regular monitoring of operating parameters such as flow rate and solution levels to maintain optimal performance. Routine inspection and maintenance of scrubber components, including pumps, nozzles, and circulation systems, are carried out to ensure consistent efficiency. This system supports effective emission control, helps maintain regulatory compliance, and contributes to environmentally responsible manufacturing practices.

Enclosed Conveyor System for Material Handling: Enclosed conveyor systems are used to transport metal dust, polishing residues, and other particulate materials within Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd., effectively minimizing airborne dust during material handling operations. These conveyors feature hermetically sealed circuits, which prevent material spillage and limit dust emissions by ensuring that materials remain fully contained throughout the transfer process. The enclosed design helps maintain workplace air quality and reduces environmental contamination by preventing the release of dust particles during material movement. In addition, it contributes to a safer working environment by minimizing employee exposure to airborne particulates. Regular monitoring is carried out to ensure proper functioning of the conveyor systems, while routine inspection and maintenance of conveyor housings, seals, transfer points, and associated components are performed to maintain optimal performance. These measures support effective dust control, improve material handling efficiency, and contribute to environmentally responsible manufacturing operations.

Dust Collectors for PM Control: Manufacturing operations at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd., including polishing, buffing, grinding, cutting, deburring, and material handling activities, are equipped with high-efficiency dust collection systems to control airborne particulate matter (PM) generated during operations. These systems use bag filters combined with pulse-jet cleaning mechanisms, which automatically remove accumulated dust from the filters and maintain consistent airflow and filtration efficiency throughout operations. The collected dust is directed into sealed containers to prevent leakage or re-entrainment into the workplace environment. These containers are periodically emptied and managed in accordance with approved waste management procedures and applicable environmental requirements. Continuous monitoring of system performance, including pressure differentials across filters and airflow rates, ensures that the dust collection units operate at optimal efficiency. Routine inspections and preventive maintenance are carried out on filter media, ducts, blowers, and collection bins to prevent blockages, reduce emissions, and maintain a safe and clean working environment. The implementation of these dust collection systems effectively minimizes worker exposure to airborne particulate matter, prevents environmental contamination, and ensures compliance with applicable air quality standards.

Delivery and Reconciliation at TSDF: On reaching the authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility (TSDF): waste is unloaded under supervision; quantity and type are verified against manifest entries; any discrepancies are documented, reported, and investigated; Form 10 is updated, signed, and one copy is returned to Kraftwares for records

These procedures are aligned with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) directives.

body.text: Hazardous waste generated during manufacturing is treated on-site using tailored methods, depending on its type and hazard level:

Neutralization Units: Used to treat acidic or alkaline wastewater and chemical residues, ensuring safe pH levels before storage or further processing.
Sludge Solidification: Sludge containing chemicals is stabilized using binding agents (like fly ash or lime) to convert it into a dry, non-leachable form suitable for secure landfilling.
Solvent Recovery and Segregation: High-value spent solvents are separated and stored for off-site recovery, reducing environmental load and enabling circular use.
Container Cleaning Units: Used chemical drums are triple-rinsed and stored safely for return to suppliers or scrap recovery vendors.
Contaminated PPE Handling: Soiled gloves, rags, and aprons are collected in labelled containers and prepared for co-processing or incineration.
All treatment processes are managed by trained EHS personnel with regular monitoring to ensure effectiveness and safety.
After treatment, hazardous waste is dispatched to CPCB/SPCB-authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs):

rows: Segregated and stored in designated containers
Sent to authorized hazardous waste facilities
Sent to metal recyclers for recovery
Reworked or recycled as metal scrap

Form 10 (Manifest): Tracks each shipment from source to disposal
Disposal Certificates and SDS records are maintained for each waste category
Annual Form IV submitted to SPCB as per compliance norms
Monthly waste reconciliation conducted to verify treatment vs. disposal ratios

Kraftwares integration of specialized treatment techniques with regulatory-compliant disposal helps reduce long-term environmental impacts and supports its broader commitment to responsible production and chemical safety.

Municipal or Approved Landfills: Non-hazardous waste, if not reused or recycled, is disposed of via local municipal waste systems or sent to government-approved landfills, in accordance with local environmental guidelines.
Recordkeeping: Disposal quantities and routes are recorded and retained to ensure traceability and compliance.

Composting & Organic Processing Units: Organic waste is sent to authorized composting sites or organic recycling facilities where it is transformed into compost or energy-rich material. This supports soil health and reduces environmental burden.
Documentation: Disposal volumes and destinations are recorded to maintain transparency and support sustainability reporting.

All review outcomes are documented, communicated to relevant teams, and followed by regular audits to maintain compliance and support continuous improvement.

blocks.text: The Sustainable Packaging Practices and Control Procedure establishes guidelines for the selection, use, and management of packaging materials at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. in an environmentally responsible manner. The procedure focuses on reducing packaging waste, promoting the use of recyclable and eco-friendly packaging materials, and optimizing packaging design to minimize environmental impacts while ensuring product protection, quality, and safe transportation. It supports efficient resource utilization and aligns packaging operations with the company's sustainability objectives and applicable regulatory requirements.

Objective
To promote the use of sustainable packaging materials and practices that reduce environmental impact while ensuring product protection, quality, and regulatory compliance.

This procedure applies to all packaging materials and activities at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. It involves procurement, production, quality assurance, warehouse, and logistics teams responsible for packaging management.

substeps.text: Packaging materials such as paper wraps, protective sleeves, cardboard cartons, corrugated boxes, and stretch wraps are selected in accordance with customer specifications, ensuring that labelling, protection, and presentation meet customer requirements.

Packaging solutions are designed to comply with transportation and export requirements while supporting Kraftwares' sustainability goals, including reducing material consumption and promoting recyclability.

Secondary and tertiary packaging are selected to ensure kitchenware products remain protected during handling, storage, and transportation while minimizing packaging waste.

Standardized packaging dimensions are followed across similar product categories to improve storage efficiency, optimize carton and pallet utilization, and reduce transportation-related impacts.
Clear recycling and disposal guidance is provided on paper wraps, cartons, and other packaging materials wherever applicable to encourage responsible waste management by customers and end-users.

Packaging materials and designs are periodically reviewed to identify opportunities for reducing packaging weight, improving recyclability, and minimizing packaging waste while maintaining product protection requirements.

Products are carefully packed using approved packaging materials in accordance with customer specifications to ensure protection against scratches, dents, and damage during storage and transportation.
Automated systems are utilized for sealing, labelling, and carton preparation wherever feasible to maintain consistency in packaging quality, reduce manual errors, and improve operational efficiency.

In-line quality checks are performed during and after packaging operations, including verification of correct product packaging, label accuracy, packaging integrity, and compliance with customer requirements.

Each carton is clearly labelled with shipment-specific details such as product codes, SKU numbers, quantity, handling instructions, and recycling symbols to support efficient logistics and responsible waste management.
All packaging waste is sorted into recyclable, reusable, and non-recyclable streams at designated collection points to support effective waste management.
Cartons, paper wraps, pallets, and suitable protective packaging materials are inspected and reused within the facility wherever feasible to reduce material consumption and environmental impact.
Non-recyclable packaging waste is handed over to authorized waste management agencies, with records maintained to ensure compliance with applicable regulations.
Scrap materials generated from packaging operations are tracked and analysed regularly to identify reduction opportunities and improve packaging efficiency.
Packaging materials and processes are continuously improved to reduce environmental impact and increase recyclability.
Employees involved in packaging operations receive training on best practices for waste reduction, material optimization, and recycling.
Routine evaluations and audits are conducted to ensure packaging practices align with Kraftwares sustainability objectives and customer requirements.

Deviations, non-conformities, and corrective actions related to packaging operations are documented and reviewed for continual improvement.

blocks.text: Kraftwares (India) Pvt. This procedure establishes a framework for evaluating, onboarding, monitoring, and engaging suppliers to ensure consistent performance and responsible sourcing throughout the supply chain.

To ensure suppliers are selected, approved, and managed through a fair, transparent, and systematic process that supports quality standards, business continuity, compliance, and responsible business practices.

This procedure applies to all suppliers, contractors, service providers, and vendors engaged by Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. for the supply of raw materials, packaging materials, machinery, spare parts, logistics services, maintenance support, and other operational requirements.

body.text: Before engagement, prospective suppliers undergo an initial evaluation to determine their suitability and capability to meet Kraftwares' business requirements.
The assessment may consider:

Product and service quality standards
Technical capability and manufacturing capacity
Regulatory compliance status
Business reputation and reliability
Occupational health and safety practices
Environmental management practices
Ethical business conduct and integrity
Suppliers may be requested to provide supporting documentation, certifications, licenses, declarations, or self-assessment information during the evaluation process.

Women-led enterprises

Small and community-based businesses

Guidance and mentoring to strengthen business, quality, and compliance capabilities

Availability of recognized certifications such as ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, GMP, or equivalent standards

Commitment to continual improvement and adoption of responsible business practices

blocks.text: The Workplace Safety and Compliance Procedure establishes a structured framework to ensure a safe and healthy working environment across all operations at Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. It outlines the responsibilities, safety practices, and compliance measures required to prevent workplace hazards, reduce the risk of accidents, and maintain adherence to applicable occupational health and safety regulations. The procedure promotes proactive safety management, employee awareness, and continuous monitoring of workplace conditions to support safe and compliant manufacturing operations.
To ensure workplace activities are conducted safely and in compliance with applicable health and safety regulations, thereby preventing accidents, injuries, and unsafe working conditions.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and visitors within Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.’s facilities. It covers safety practices, hazard identification, compliance requirements, and monitoring of workplace conditions across manufacturing, polishing, pressing, welding, assembly, storage, warehouse, maintenance, and administrative areas.

Only trained and authorized personnel may operate material-handling equipment such as forklifts, pallet trucks, hand trolleys, hydraulic stackers, and lifting equipment used for handling stainless steel sheets, coils, components, raw materials, and finished products.

Use mechanical lifting aids for heavy metal sheets, coils, dies, finished products, and bulk materials to avoid manual overexertion.

Store raw materials, stainless steel sheets, components, consumables, packaging materials, and finished goods in clearly labelled containers, designated storage areas, or approved racking systems.

Use ergonomic workstations and appropriate handling aids during packaging and dispatch activities.
Dispose of packaging waste such as paper, cardboard, plastic films, straps, and wrapping materials only in designated collection bins.

Ensure correct labelling, coding, and documentation of all finished products before storage or dispatch.

Switch off machinery, equipment, and electrical devices when not in use or during maintenance activities.
Report any sparking, overheating, burning smell, damaged wiring, or abnormal equipment noise immediately to the Maintenance Team.
Keep electrical panels accessible at all times and ensure surrounding areas remain dry and free from obstructions.

Ensure trucks, containers, and transport vehicles are fully stationary and secured before loading or unloading materials and finished products.
Do not stand beneath suspended loads during lifting or material movement operations.
Use wheel chocks, dock levelers, and other safety devices where applicable.
Maintain a safe distance from moving forklifts, pallet trucks, cranes, and other material-handling equipment.
Ensure materials and finished goods are stacked evenly and secured properly to prevent tipping, shifting, or damage during transportation.

Ensure safe handling, storage, and use of chemicals, lubricants, adhesives, coatings, cleaning agents, and other substances used in manufacturing and maintenance activities.
Maintain up-to-date Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS/SDS) for all hazardous substances at accessible locations.
Use appropriate PPE such as chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, face shields, aprons, and masks when handling chemicals.
Ensure adequate ventilation and local exhaust systems in areas involving chemical usage, coating, welding, polishing, or cleaning operations.
Clearly label all chemical containers and never store chemicals in unmarked containers.
Store chemicals in designated, well-ventilated areas away from heat sources and ignition points.
Follow all training instructions related to chemical handling, spill response, and emergency procedures.
Use spill control kits immediately in the event of leaks or spills and report incidents to the supervisor.
Eating, drinking, and smoking are strictly prohibited in chemical storage and handling areas.

Keep floors clean and dry at all times; immediately clean water, oil, grease, or chemical spills.
Use anti-slip mats in high-traffic areas, production zones, and loading/unloading areas where required.
Ensure adequate lighting in manufacturing areas, warehouses, storage rooms, stairways, and walkways.
Use handrails when using stairs, platforms, or elevated walkways.
Secure loose cables, hoses, straps, packaging materials, and tools away from pedestrian pathways.
Do not climb on pallets, racks, machinery, material stacks, or unstable surfaces.
Use approved ladders or work platforms when accessing elevated storage locations and ensure stability before use.
Wear safety shoes with slip-resistant soles in all operational and production areas.

Immediately clean metal dust, polishing residues, oil spills, and material scraps to prevent slip hazards and maintain a safe working environment.
Keep emergency exits, fire extinguishers, electrical panels, and walkways clear at all times.
Maintain cleanliness in rest areas, canteen facilities, and workstations; wash hands before meals and after handling materials or chemicals.
Dispose of waste only in designated bins as per Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.’s Waste Management Procedure.

Inform supervisors immediately if feeling unwell, fatigued, or experiencing discomfort due to dust, fumes, chemical exposure, or work conditions.
Take scheduled rest breaks to reduce fatigue during repetitive manufacturing, polishing, assembly, or material-handling activities.
Stay adequately hydrated, especially during physically demanding tasks or hot weather conditions.
Use appropriate PPE such as dust masks, gloves, safety glasses, or respirators (where required) when handling chemicals, polishing compounds, metal dust, or other materials.

Ensure workstations, assembly tables, polishing stations, inspection areas, and packing tables are maintained at appropriate working heights.
Maintain neutral posture with a straight back, relaxed shoulders, and properly aligned wrists during work activities.
Use chairs with adequate back support and footrests where prolonged seated work is required for inspection, documentation, or packing activities.

Rotate employees between assembly, polishing, inspection, packaging, and material-handling tasks to reduce repetitive strain.
Take short stretching breaks every 30–60 minutes to relieve strain on shoulders, wrists, hands, and back.
Encourage brief walking breaks for employees engaged in prolonged standing or seated activities.

Use ergonomically designed hand tools and equipment with comfortable grips to minimize strain during manufacturing and assembly operations.
Keep tools, materials, and components within easy reach to avoid excessive stretching or awkward movements.
Ensure adequate lighting and visual aids are available for detailed inspection and quality control activities.

Avoid excessive force while operating tools, handling materials, polishing products, or packing finished goods.
Keep wrists straight and avoid repetitive twisting motions during assembly and finishing activities.
Follow the 20-20-20 eye rule when performing prolonged inspection, documentation, or computer-based work.

Do not tamper with machine guards, safety devices, or protective barriers.
Keep work areas clean and free from obstructions, particularly in production, storage, and dispatch zones.
Report unsafe conditions, near misses, spills, equipment defects, or incidents immediately.
Follow floor markings, safety signage, and designated work zones.
Smoking, horseplay, running within operational areas, and misuse of equipment are strictly prohibited.

Head Protection: Safety helmets in material storage, loading/unloading, and overhead handling areas where required.
Hand Protection: Cut-resistant gloves, handling gloves, or chemical-resistant gloves depending on the task performed.
Foot Protection: Safety shoes mandatory in all operational areas.
Eye Protection: Safety glasses or goggles during cutting, grinding, polishing, welding, and material handling activities.
Body Protection: High-visibility jackets and protective workwear where applicable.
Hearing Protection: Earplugs or earmuffs in designated high-noise areas.

Report all incidents, including minor injuries, cuts, burns, falls, chemical splashes, equipment-related incidents, or near misses to the supervisor immediately. The Safety Officer shall investigate incidents and implement corrective actions.
All incidents shall be recorded, reviewed, and discussed during periodic safety meetings.

Non-compliance with safety requirements may result in disciplinary action, including warnings, retraining, or suspension depending on the severity of the violation.
All safety procedures shall be reviewed annually or earlier following major incidents, audit findings, operational changes, or regulatory updates.
Employees are encouraged to provide suggestions for improving workplace safety and operational practices.

blocks.text: Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. is committed to maintaining a safe and prepared working environment through the provision and management of emergency response resources. This procedure establishes the requirements for identifying, installing, monitoring, maintaining, and replenishing emergency equipment throughout the facility to support an effective response to workplace emergencies and minimize risks to employees, visitors, assets, and operations.

The objective of this procedure is to ensure that emergency equipment remains available, accessible, operational, and suitable for responding to incidents such as fires, injuries, electrical emergencies, chemical spills, and other unforeseen events that may occur within the workplace.
This procedure applies to all manufacturing, polishing, assembly, packaging, warehouse, storage, maintenance, utility, dispatch, and office areas operated by Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.

It covers all emergency response resources maintained within the facility, including firefighting equipment, first aid facilities, spill response materials, emergency lighting systems, and evacuation support equipment.

body.text: Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd. identifies emergency equipment requirements through periodic workplace hazard assessments conducted by the EHS Department in consultation with operational departments.
Emergency response resources are allocated considering:

The nature of manufacturing and support activities performed within each area.
The number of employees working in the area.
Potential fire, electrical, chemical, and machinery-related hazards.
Ease of accessibility during emergency situations.
Applicable legal and safety requirements.

Safety signs, equipment identification labels, and directional markings are displayed to help employees quickly locate emergency resources. Routine inspections are carried out by designated EHS personnel on a monthly basis to verify that emergency equipment remains available and operational.
Inspections typically include verification of:

Physical condition of equipment.
Functional readiness.
Accessibility and visibility.
Condition of safety signage.
Expiry dates where applicable.
Availability of all required components and accessories.

Inspection findings are documented using standardized checklists and equipment inspection records. Any deficiencies identified during inspections are communicated to the responsible department and corrective actions are initiated promptly to restore equipment readiness.
Kraftwares maintains a preventive maintenance program for emergency equipment to ensure reliability during emergency situations.
Fire extinguishers undergo:

Monthly visual inspections.
Periodic servicing by authorized service providers.

This procedure applies to all production machinery, polishing equipment, material handling equipment, hand tools, electrical equipment, utility systems, and other operational assets used within Kraftwares (India) Pvt. Ltd.
It also applies to all employees, contractors, and visitors who are required to use personal protective equipment while performing activities within operational areas.

responsibilities: Oversees the implementation of equipment safety inspections and audits.

Ensure employees use appropriate protective equipment.
Adhere to safety guidelines and properly use protective equipment.

body.text: Kraftwares conducts periodic inspections of machinery, tools, and equipment to identify potential safety concerns before they result in incidents or operational disruptions.

Production machinery
Polishing and finishing equipment
Material handling equipment
Electrical installations
Portable tools
Utility systems

Overall operational condition.
Structural stability and integrity.

Alignment, calibration, and operational performance.
Housekeeping and safe access around equipment.
Compliance with applicable safety requirements.
Inspection findings are recorded and reviewed by the responsible departments.
Any unsafe condition or equipment deficiency identified during inspections is documented and assigned for corrective action.
Actions may include:

Equipment repair
Component replacement
Maintenance intervention
Additional operator training
Engineering controls
Equipment presenting significant safety risks is isolated from operation until corrective measures are completed and safe operating conditions are restored.
Follow-up verification is conducted to confirm closure of identified issues.

sops.title: Procedure for Compliance Approval of Sensitive Transactions

blocks.text: This procedure establishes guidelines for obtaining approval, reporting, and managing high-risk transactions at Kraftwares, including charitable donations, sponsorships, procurement of raw materials and packaging, gifts, and business travel, ensuring compliance with company policies and ethical standards.

body.text: Determine if the transaction falls under sensitive transactions. Sensitive transactions include gifts, travel, hospitality, charitable donations, supplier contracts, and high-value procurement activities.

Submit for approval to the Ethics Compliance Officer. Transactions must be reported in person or via email at ethics.compliance@kraftwares.com with full context and justification. High-value or high-risk transactions require a formal request.

Maintain complete records of approved transactions. Records must include purpose, participants, expenses, and approval documentation. All supporting documents must be attached to procurement or expense reports.
Conduct a post-approval ethical review. Confirm that the transaction is documented transparently and does not create risks of undue influence, conflicts of interest, or bribery.

sops.title: Procedure for Confidential Data Handling and Breach Responses

blocks.text: This procedure establishes guidelines for managing confidential information, ensuring data security, and responding to breaches. It includes data classification, secure handling, access controls, incident detection, and response protocols to protect Kraftwares’ and third-party data from unauthorized access or disclosure.

body.text: Data Classification: Data must be categorized as follows:

rows: Highly sensitive data requiring strict access controls (e.g., personal data, financial records)
Data critical to business operations but not classified as confidential (e.g., employee records, operational processes)
Information intended for public dissemination (e.g., marketing materials, press releases)

body.text: Access Control:

Access is granted based on the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP), ensuring employees only have the necessary permissions for their roles.
Roles and responsibilities are clearly defined, with appropriate access levels assigned accordingly.
The Data Protection Officer (DPO) conducts quarterly access reviews using automated logs and manual checks to ensure compliance with access policies.
Non-compliant access is immediately revoked, investigated, and corrective actions are taken, followed by a compliance review.

Confidential information are stored in secure environments e.g., locked file cabinets and secure servers such as cloud-based servers to guarantee encryption and regulatory compliance.
Transmission of confidential data is conducted via secure channels i.e. VPNs and encrypted emails.
All confidential data are encrypted both in transit and at rest, following appropriate encryption protocols suitable for the company’s data security requirements.
Access to storage areas containing confidential data is restricted to authorized personnel.
Access control systems i.e. keycards is used to manage physical access.

substeps.text: Identification: For IT Department — System logs are records generated by operating systems, applications, or network devices that provide a detailed history of events, activities, and transactions occurring within a system. Regularly analyze system logs for unusual access patterns and failed login attempts to monitor for signs of data breaches.

Identification: For Employee — Employees are responsible for reporting any unusual system behavior, unauthorized access attempts, or suspicious activities observed during their work. Prompt reporting enables the IT department to investigate and respond to potential data incidents in a timely manner. Regularly analyze system logs for unusual access patterns and failed login attempts to monitor for signs of data breaches.

Reporting: Employees must report any suspected data breaches immediately to their supervisor and the IT department. An incident reporting form must be filled out and submitted to the IT department for documentation.
Escalation Protocol: Depending on the severity, escalate incidents to management and legal counsel as necessary.

Containment: The IT Security manager will immediately isolate affected systems to prevent further unauthorized access. This team is responsible for implementing containment measures, which may include disconnecting the affected systems from the network, disabling user accounts, or restricting access until a thorough investigation is conducted and the issue is resolved.

Investigation: The Incident Response Team (IRT) will conduct a thorough investigation to determine the cause and impact of the breach. They will collect relevant logs and evidence, analyze data to identify vulnerabilities, and assess the breach's extent. Interviews with personnel may be conducted for additional insights. The team will document findings and prepare an incident report with recommendations for remediation. This approach helps prevent similar incidents in the future.

Communication: Affected stakeholders will be notified via email or formal communication channels, detailing the nature of the breach, affected data, and potential risks. Guidance will include recommended actions to protect their information, such as changing passwords and monitoring for suspicious activities. Regular updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

Internal Communication: Management and the legal team are kept informed through scheduled progress updates, including regular emails being sent on their respective official email-ids, meetings, and incident reports. All critical developments, decisions, and actions are documented and communicated in a timely manner to ensure alignment and compliance throughout the process.

Remediation: Corrective actions including revising data access controls, enhancing encryption protocols, updating security policies, providing targeted employee retraining, and improving incident detection systems are taken. These measures are designed to address vulnerabilities identified during the investigation and prevent similar breaches in the future.

Post-Incident Review: A review meeting is conducted by the Incident Response Team, led by the IT Security Manager to analyze response effectiveness and identify improvements by enhancing communication protocols, refining the incident response process and upgrading security monitoring tools.
Documentation Retention: Maintain detailed records of the incident, including timelines, actions taken, and any communications for at least three years.

Regular Review: The IT Security Officer, will review and update the procedures annually or following significant incidents to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with evolving security threats and legal requirements.

sops.title: Securing Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access

blocks.text: To protect sensitive information shared with or received from third parties by implementing robust access controls, ensuring data privacy, and mitigating risks of unauthorized data exposure.

body.text: Access controls are implemented to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive third-party data. Utilize Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) are considered to restrict access according to employees' job roles and responsibilities.

Third-party data is encrypted during transmission using secure protocols and at rest with appropriate encryption methods. Encryption keys are stored securely, granting access based on the need-to-know principle.
Third-party data are stored on secure, access-controlled encrypted servers and regular reviews of access permissions to ensure compliance with data protection policies are conducted

Third-party data are shared through secure methods such as encrypted email or secure file transfer protocols (SFTP). The identity and authorization of recipients are verified before sharing sensitive information, and maintain logs of all data-sharing activities, including recipient details and timestamps.

Third parties handling or accessing sensitive data have signed a Data Protection Agreement (DPA), outlining their obligations for safeguarding information. Contracts include clauses that mandate the implementation of equivalent security measures and the prompt reporting of any data breaches.

blocks.text: Regular training sessions are conducted for employees on data protection practices, including the proper handling and sharing of third-party data. Employees are aware of their responsibilities and the consequences of failing to protect third-party data.

narrative.text: Monitoring systems are in place to detect any unauthorized access or attempts to access third-party data. Regular audits of data access logs, storage practices, and third-party compliance are conducted to identify and rectify potential security gaps.

body.text: In case of a data breach involving third-party information, the Incident Response Procedure is followed to contain and mitigate the breach. Affected third parties are promptly notified, provided with breach details, potential impacts, and the corrective actions taken.

sops.title: Stakeholder Consent and Data Processing Retention and Disposal

blocks.text: To ensure that data is handled in compliance with stakeholder permissions, maintaining appropriate data retention periods and secure disposal practices to uphold privacy standards and regulatory requirements.

body.text: Consent is obtained through formal mechanisms through signed consent form and digital agreements. These documents clearly outline the purpose of data collection, how the data will be used, and stakeholders rights. Additionally, a confirmation process through email verification and electronic signature is used to ensure stakeholders have fully understood the terms before granting their consent.

Stakeholders are provided with clear information which is communicated through a Privacy Notice which outlines how data will be used, the retention periods, and the stakeholders rights regarding their data, including access, correction, or deletion. These documents are provided at the point of data collection, either in print or digital form.

Establishing Retention Timelines: Each type of data is categorized based on its sensitivity and relevance, with specific retention timelines defined according to legal requirements, business needs, or contractual obligations.

body.text: Tracking Retention Periods: Appropriate data management systems are utilized to track the retention period of stored data, ensuring that data is flagged for review or deletion once the retention period expires.

Secure Disposal: Once data is no longer required, it is securely deleted using methods appropriate to its sensitivity. For digital data, secure deletion methods such as data wiping or cryptographic erasure are used. For physical data, documents are shredded or incinerated in a controlled environment.
Compliance Checks: Regular audits are conducted to ensure that data is retained or disposed of in accordance with the established policies and legal requirements.

Regular Audits: The Data Protection Officer (DPO) will conduct the annual audits of data access and handling practices. The audit will be conducted through a systematic review process, including examining access logs, evaluating data handling procedures, interviewing relevant personnel, and assessing compliance with established policies. Additionally, random sampling of data access and handling activities may be performed to ensure adherence to standards.

Continuous Monitoring: Appropriate monitoring controls are maintained to detect unauthorized access and anomalies in data access patterns, in line with the company’s IT infrastructure and security capabilities.
